transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start off, can you tell me what's been bringing you in to see me?

Hi. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, and I really don't want to overreact or waste your time. It's just... I've been feeling pretty overwhelmed lately, and what finally scared me enough to actually come in is... well, I keep having these thoughts. 

Just thinking that maybe it would be easier if I just didn't wake up. Which I know sounds awful, I'm sorry. But sometimes, when I'm driving home from the clinic—I'm a vet tech—I'll just catch myself looking at the road and wondering what would happen if I just... didn't turn the wheel. 

I know that's probably not a normal way to think, so I thought I should probably talk to someone. Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I came in for that.
How long have you been feeling this way—when did these overwhelmed feelings and thoughts about not waking up first start?

Um... I guess it's been about a month? We recently had to take in a relative, and... well, it's just been this really intense, up-and-down sort of crisis at home ever since. I really don't want to make it sound like I'm complaining about my family, because I know I should be able to handle it, but... yeah, that's when things got so overwhelming and those thoughts started creeping in. About a month ago. 

Is that the kind of information you need? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions okay.
Over this past month, have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest and pleasure in things you normally enjoy, most of the day, nearly every day?

Well... yes, I suppose I have. I try really hard to keep a positive attitude for my family, especially with the house being so chaotic right now, but... honestly, most days it just feels like the color has completely drained out of everything. 

Even when everyone is bustling around me, I just feel this heavy sadness. I'm actually a little embarrassed to admit this, but... sometimes I end up hiding in the laundry room just to cry. I just... I can't stand the thought of anyone seeing me like that and realizing how hopeless I've been feeling. I know I should be holding it together better for them, so I try to keep it hidden. 

Does that... does that answer your question okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Besides the sadness, have you noticed changes in your sleep, appetite, energy, or ability to concentrate over this past month?

Um... well, my sleep has definitely been a little off. I hope it's okay to mention this, I know it's probably just stress from the house being so full, but... I've been having a really hard time actually sleeping. 

I'll just lie there in the dark, and my brain just keeps replaying every little thing I've done wrong that day, or I'll wake up hours before my alarm and just feel completely drained. I've been trying to just stay in bed a little longer to rest, but... honestly, I'm still so exhausted I haven't even been able to go for my morning runs, which I know is terrible. I really should be pushing through it better. 

I haven't really noticed much with my appetite or concentration, though. Just the sleep and feeling so tired. Is... is that the kind of detail you were looking for? I hope I'm not overcomplicating things.
Have you ever had a period like this before—weeks of persistent sadness, low energy, or trouble sleeping—at any other time in your life, even before this recent family stress?

Um... well... I really hate to admit this, because I know I should have gotten a handle on it by myself a long time ago. But... yes. It actually started quite a while before all this recent family stress. 

I guess... well, this heavy feeling has been hanging over me for about 11 months now? I kept telling myself I was just a little burned out from work, but... yeah, even before this past month made everything feel so completely unbearable, it was there. 

I'm sorry, I hope it's okay that I didn't mention that right away. I just feel a little foolish letting it go on for so long without fixing it myself. Is... is that the kind of timeline you needed to know? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture.
Over these past 11 months, was there ever a stretch of two months or more where you felt completely back to your normal self, without the sadness or low energy, before things got worse again?

Um... no, not really. I mean, I try to have good days, you know? I really try to put on a brave face and just push through it, especially at the clinic where the animals and the owners need me to be upbeat. But... if I'm being completely honest, which I know I need to be... that heavy feeling hasn't ever fully gone away for that long. 

There were maybe a few days here and there where I felt a tiny bit lighter, but definitely not two whole months. It's just sort of been this constant, low-level drain in the background this whole time. I'm sorry, I know I should be stronger than this and just snap out of it. I really have been trying. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it right.
You mentioned having these thoughts about not waking up or not turning the wheel—how often are these thoughts occurring, and have you ever thought about a specific way you might act on them?

Um... well, it's... I really don't want to alarm you, and I know it sounds terrible, but... it's been happening a little more often lately. That's actually what finally scared me enough to make an appointment. 

I just... I keep thinking it would be so much easier if I just didn't wake up in the morning. And... um... sometimes when I'm driving home from the clinic, when I'm just so tired, I catch myself wondering what would happen if I just... didn't turn the wheel on a curve. 

But I haven't made any real plans or anything like that! I promise I wouldn't actually do anything to hurt myself, I know how much that would devastate my family. It's just... these passing thoughts that sneak up on me. I really hope you don't think I'm crazy for saying that. Is it... is it normal to have thoughts like that when you're this exhausted?
Over this past month, have you been feeling unusually worthless, or experiencing excessive guilt about things, even minor things that wouldn't normally bother you this much?

Um... well... I feel awful even admitting this, because I know I should be more understanding. But... yes. I've been feeling so terribly guilty lately. 

With all the stress at home right now, I just... I keep telling myself I'm a terrible person for resenting the disruption. I try so hard to be patient and helpful, but then I'll catch myself giving a sharp look or making a slightly impatient comment, and... I just replay it in my head over and over again. It makes me feel like such a burden, like... like my husband and my family would honestly just be better off without me dragging them down. 

I'm so sorry, I know that sounds so selfish and ungrateful of me. I really am trying to be a better, more supportive person for them. Do... do you think that makes me a bad person for feeling that way? I just want to be good for them.

Um... no, I don't think so. I haven't really noticed anything like that at all. 

I'm sorry, I hope that's okay to say. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the information you need. If I'm misunderstanding what you mean, please let me know. I really want to be helpful... did I answer that correctly?

Um... no, I haven't. I'm sorry, I feel like I should have a better answer for you, but I really haven't experienced anything like that. 

I hope I'm not being difficult or unhelpful! I just want to be completely honest with you so you have the right information to go on. Is it... is it normal that I haven't noticed that? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and giving you what you need.

I haven't touched my camera at all lately. And I haven't checked the bird feeders with any real interest, or even cared about what’s coming up in the garden. 

It's actually a little frightening to admit that out loud, because those things used to be how I felt like myself. I hope that doesn't make me sound terrible or lazy. I know I should be making more of an effort to do the things I love... does that make sense? I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for.

But I want to be completely honest with you, so... no, I haven't experienced that. I really hope I'm still being helpful.
Over this past month, have you had trouble concentrating, focusing on tasks, or making everyday decisions—like at work with the animals or paperwork?

Um... well, I've really been trying to stay on top of everything at the clinic. The animals need me, and I'd hate to make a mistake that causes extra work for the rest of the staff. But... if I'm being perfectly honest, yes, it has been a bit of a struggle lately. 

I just find myself reading the same chart three times before the information actually sticks. And even simple things, like deciding which supplies to restock first... it just feels like my brain is wading through mud. I've been double-checking everything because I'm so terrified of messing up. 

I'm so sorry, I know that probably sounds like I'm not doing my job very well right now. I really am trying my hardest to push through it and stay focused. Is it normal to feel this scattered? I hope I'm not letting everyone down too much by being like this.

Um... I don't think so? I mean, I'm trying to think back, but nothing really comes to mind. 

I'm sorry, I know you're asking about all these different things to get a complete picture, and I want to give you all the information you need. I just... I really haven't experienced that. I hope that's an okay answer? I worry sometimes that if I keep saying no, it might seem like I'm not paying enough attention to myself, but I promise I'm trying to be as accurate as I can for you. Am I doing okay with these questions?
Over this past month, have you or others noticed you moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or conversely, feeling unusually restless or fidgety and unable to sit still?

Um... no, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I try to keep a pretty steady pace, especially at work where everyone relies on me. I haven't had anyone say anything to me about moving slow or... or being too fidgety. 

I really hope I'm not missing something that I should have picked up on. I know you're trying to figure out what's going on with me, and I want to be a good patient and give you the right answers. But, um, as far as I know, my moving and speaking have just been... normal, I think? Does that make sense? I'm sorry if that's not very helpful.
